newsitem.title: MALTA: EU launches Mediterranean key indicators service.
newsitem.headline: EU launches Mediterranean key indicators service.

text.p: The European Union is launching a bulletin of Mediterranean key economic indicators to help potential investors make informed decisions about the region.
Eurostat, the EU's statistical office, said in a statement on Tuesday that the bulletin would be published twice this year and become a quarterly in 1997.

"The availability of reliable, comparable and accessible statistical information will be an essential element in strengthening the dialogue and exchanges between the Euro- Mediterranean partners," said Eurostat director-general Yves Franchet.
The first issue of the bulletin -- timed to coincide with a Malta meeting of EU and Mediterranean foreign ministers -- lists GDP figures, tourism numbers, unemployment data and trade statistics.
The latest figures available, however, are only for 1995.
They show Malta enjoyed the highest GDP growth of the Mediterranean countries -- a provisional 9.6 percent -- followed by Turkey with 7.2 percent and Israel with 7.1 percent.
Algeria had the highest unemployment rate -- 28.1 percent -- while Cyprus boasted the lowest, 2.6 percent.
The Eurostat bulletin said Turkey's inflation rate in 1995 was 93.6 percent, while Jordan registered 2.3 percent.
The statistical bulletin has been launched to boost economic cooperation between the EU and Mediterranean under the so-called Euro-Med dialogue which aims also to boost political and economic links.
Represented in the programme are Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Israel, the Palestinian Authority, Cyprus, Malta and Turkey.
